operations.evidence: Of the 67 convicted persons, 39, or 58%, pleaded guilty.
Plea distributions do not establish local public-safety conditions.
Of the 67 convicted persons, 28, or 42%, entered a not-guilty plea.
A plea category is a court-process measure and not parcel evidence.
There were 273 persons in custody for terrorism and terrorism-connected offences in Great Britain on 31 March 2026.
Custody totals do not identify where offences occurred or local risk.
The custody total was seven higher than the 266 recorded on 31 March 2025.
A national custody change cannot be assigned to neighbourhoods or parcels.
The Metropolitan Police Service stopped and searched 98 persons under section 43 of the Terrorism Act 2000.
The count covers a police-force area and excludes vehicle-only searches.
The 98 MPS section 43 stops were 36% higher than the 72 in the previous year.
The annual change is not a parcel-level exposure rate.
Other police forces in England and Wales reported a further 108 section 43 stops.
These newly collected figures are official statistics in development and have data-quality limitations.
Sixteen arrests resulted from MPS section 43 stop and searches in the year ending 31 March 2026.
An arrest following a stop does not establish guilt or local parcel risk.
Other police forces in England and Wales reported 22 arrests resulting from section 43 stops.
The figures are under development and are not suitable for precise local scoring.
Of 2,819 linked arrests, 484 were charged, 36 were released without charge, 12 had alternative action and 2,287 were bailed to return or released under investigation.
Many cases remained unresolved, so outcome proportions can change.
At the data cutoff, 484 of the 2,819 linked arrests, or 21%, had resulted in a charge.
The rate is provisional because many cases were still progressing.
The linked charges included 8 under section 12 and 473 under section 13 of the Terrorism Act 2000.
Legislative charge counts do not establish conviction or property-level risk.
Of the 484 linked charges, 456 were awaiting prosecution.
Awaiting-prosecution cases are incomplete and may have different final outcomes.
Twenty-five of the 484 linked charges had other outcomes.
The broad outcome category combines different resolutions and is not comparable to conviction.
Three of the 484 linked charges were not proceeded against.
Small case counts must not be used for parcel inference.
Among 2,814 linked arrests where sex was known, 1,368 were male, 1,445 female and one non-binary.
Demographic aggregates must not be used to profile individuals or locations.
Among linked arrests with known age, 2,561, or 91%, were aged 30 or above.
Age composition is not a measure of neighbourhood risk.
The average age was 59 for linked arrests and 31 for all other arrests.
Average ages conceal variation and must not support individual or parcel inference.
The reported age range was 17 to 89 for linked arrests and 13 to 70 for all other arrests.
Minimum and maximum ages are descriptive and not predictive.
Where ethnic appearance was known, 1,738 of 1,800 linked arrests, or 97%, were recorded as White by the arresting officer.
Officer-recorded appearance is not self-defined ethnicity and must not be used for profiling.
